name: Zucchini
why_now: Zucchini is abundantly available through August and at its best when small to medium sized — the larger ones that appear later in the season can be watery. Right now they're quick to cook, mild enough to take on other flavors, and cheap enough to use without planning precisely.
how_to_choose: Small to medium — 6 to 8 inches is ideal; larger ones are often seedy and watery
The ends should look fresh, not dry or shriveled
buy_this_much: 3–4 medium zucchini. They cook down significantly, so buy more than you think you need.
price_note: Zucchini is very inexpensive in August — often one of the lowest-cost items in the basket. Any grocery store will have them.

flavor_paths.name: Charred
flavor_paths.description: In a smoking pan until the edges blacken.

flavor_paths.name: Sautéed fast
flavor_paths.description: Golden at the edges, basil at the end.

flavor_paths.name: Shaved raw
flavor_paths.description: Ribbons with olive oil, lime, and flaky salt.

weekday_uses: Charred in coins for the charred plate
Sautéed fast for a rice bowl
On the sheet pan with drumsticks
weekend_use: Shaved raw into ribbons with olive oil, lime, and flaky salt, beside the pork chops.
storage: Refrigerator crisper, up to a week. Don't wash before storing.
one_thing_to_learn: Zucchini releases a lot of water. To avoid a soggy pan, don't crowd them — cook in a single layer with space between pieces, and don't stir too often. High heat and patience are the technique. Once the water has cooked off, what's left will actually brown.
market_question: Do you have any smaller zucchini? Or yellow squash?
